northStar: Evidence beside verdict. A grade is never shown without the reason it can be checked against. Apple's clarity, deference and depth, applied to a tool people use under deadline pressure.

materials.rule: Applied only where content genuinely scrolls underneath; degrades to an opaque token without backdrop-filter support.

motion.rule: State only — change, feedback, loading, reveal. No orchestrated page-load sequence in the app; the marketing page's one authored moment plays once and rests. Bounce and elastic easing are not in the system.

breakpoints.rule: Responsive behaviour is structural (collapse, restack, truncate), never fluid type.

browserSurfaces.rule: The surfaces the browser draws still belong to the design system.

accessibility.standard: WCAG 2.1 AA, held in both themes
accessibility.verified: Every foreground/background pair checked against its own surface per theme; grade fills checked against their ink; chart ramps validated for lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation and surface contrast, per theme.
accessibility.knownLimit: Light chart ramp: blue vs purple is close under protanopia when all five series render simultaneously and unlabelled. Legend plus direct labels required beyond four simultaneous unordered series; otherwise facet.
accessibility.colorNeverAlone: Grades carry a letter; rule results carry a label and icon; voice states carry readable text.
accessibility.reducedMotion: Honoured, including the assistant voice orb.

notCanonized: The dashboard's four-across stat-tile row is the incumbent composition, retained because this pass was scoped to the visual layer. It is not a pattern to reproduce on new surfaces; it is the hero-metric template the craft floor warns about.

`--warning-foreground` used as a text colour on the page ground was a shipped defect (near-black in both themes, invisible on dark). It was repaired in EligibilityList and the warning badge, and the rule is now recorded — but the token pattern is not a system rule to copy.

The bare `d` keypress that toggles the theme is an incumbent behaviour with no discoverability; it is now surfaced in the theme control's tooltip, but a global single-letter hotkey is not a pattern the system endorses.
